title: Code and derived tables for: Species abundance is not a gene dose — a two-constraint criterion for functional inference in metagenomics

creators.name: He, Wanli
creators.affiliation: School of Medicine, Shangqiu Institute of Technology

description:
Version 1.0.8 makes the one script the text names by name agree with the table it is cited for, and says where to get the input the deposit leaves out. review_final.py recomputed the conditional threshold from a single seed while Table 4 and Figure 1 report medians, so its Table 4 section printed ratios of 1.65, 3.57 and 2.36 where the table says 1.6, 4.0 and 3.4; section 5.8 of the manuscript points readers to that section as the place those numbers come from. Sections 1 and 7 now read hstar_median.json. Section 4 keeps the single-seed threshold on purpose, because the 3.3-4.0 interval quoted in section 3.2 is computed from it and the sentence that follows gives the spread over eight seeds. The script also wrote review_response.txt on every run; that file is not part of the deposit, so running the script put it back, one git add away from the archive. It now writes final_numbers.txt, which is excluded along with the old name. Finally, ELDERMET_species_189x836.csv is not redistributed here, and eight of the fourteen scripts that read it failed on a clean download instead of saying so; README section 5 now gives the file it comes from, the worksheet to take, and the checksums that show the rebuild is byte-for-byte identical, and review_final.py prints the same three lines when the file is absent. No measurement, threshold or verdict changes.

Version 1.0.7 finishes the housekeeping that Version 1.0.6 began. Five scripts still described their purpose in terms of a reviewer request; the docstrings now state what each script tests, which is what a reader of the deposit needs and all that the archive should carry. No code path, input or output changes.

Version 1.0.6 makes the figures read their numbers from the tables. Figure 1 carried the family detection rate λdet as three constants typed into make_figures.py, computed before the genome-size correction that Version 1.0.4 applied to the manuscript and to Table 3; once those two moved, the figure kept the earlier values, so the rate printed beside C. perfringens disagreed with the tabulated one. make_figures.py and eff_calibration.py now sum λ from lambda_v2.tsv and derive the depth required for λdet = 5 from the same sum, so figure, calibration log and Table 3 cannot drift apart again; §3 of eff_calibration.txt was recomputed on that basis. The release also drops a working note that had travelled with the deposit since v1.0.0 and belongs to internal correspondence rather than to a public archive, normalises the apostrophe in the Xi’an cohort label so that the label joins across Table S1 and Table S3, and gives the depth annotation its provenance in the figure script rather than leaving it as a literal. No measurement or verdict changed: every table, threshold and ratio is as in Version 1.0.5.

Version 1.0.5 makes Table S1 auditable row by row. TableS1_threshold_detail.tsv now carries two further counts for every cohort-setting: contributing_species, the number of catalogue carriers with non-zero cohort-mean abundance, and ratio_nsp, the family size at which H/H* was actually evaluated. The older file quoted that ratio on all four family-size rows of a cohort, which reads as a flat threshold rather than a single evaluation; the two counts make the distinction checkable. In ELDERMET, for instance, 20 catalogue carriers are matched but only 5 contribute abundance, so the quoted ratio of 1.63 belongs to the nsp = 20 row. Recomputing every cohort at its contributing count changes no verdict. The release adds add_s1_columns.py, which recomputes both counts from the per-cohort abundance matrices and cross-checks each ratio against H(nsp = ratio_nsp)/H* at that size; all forty cells agree.

Version 1.0.4 aligns the deposit with the manuscript text. lambda_v2.py now takes the detection efficiency calibrated on the endogenous rpoB control (ε = 0.71, range 0.48–0.94) instead of the retired 1/6 reading-frame argument, uses the finished Clostridium perfringens ATCC 13124 chromosome (CP000246, 3,256,683 bp) for the genome size, and prints both sensitivity grids, in ε and in genome size; review_final.py carries the same constant. The release also adds m6_discriminant.py and Table S5, the family-by-family test of whether the dispersion statistic H carries information beyond the weighted mean carriage ceff, computed on 10,104 sub-families of real hdcA carrier sets.

Analysis code and derived tables for a manuscript that bounds the substitution of species abundance for gene-family abundance in metagenomic functional inference.

The deposit contains the simulation that calibrates the fidelity constraint H, the threshold tables across ten cohort-settings, the detection-efficiency calibration and the prospective read-level test for histidine decarboxylase (hdcA), and a genome-by-genome carriage analysis for bile salt hydrolase (Pfam PF02275) used as a positive control.

Version 1.0.3 sets the record metadata from this file, so later releases carry it automatically. Version 1.0.2 adds the single-species sensitivity test of section 5.10 to gen_bsh_table.py. Version 1.0.1 added domain_carriage.py, gen_bsh_table.py and Table S4 (bile salt hydrolase carriage in eleven ELDERMET species). Version 1.0.0 contains the rest. Requires Python 3.13 and pyhmmer 0.12.3; see README.md for the command that regenerates each table and figure.
